review_evidence: Codex self-review: focus-theme alignment, original prose and verse, evidence-backed reading, contextual tense work, and own-words production
Focused checks: canonical hash, key-option consistency, passage freshness, assessment coverage, and chapter/corpus quality
title: One Thing at a Time
source_note: NCERT structural alignment only. Zidd uses original teaching passages, checks, and feedback instead of copying the textbook body.

levels.title: Find the focus message and evidence
levels.focus: identify a paragraph or short poem's main idea and support it
levels.teaching_goal: State the broad message about focused effort and cite a detail showing its effect.

guided_check.teaching_block: A main idea explains all the details. Closing extra tabs, finishing the diagram, and then replying all support the message that one task at a time improves work.
guided_check.passage: Mohan tried to answer messages while drawing a food-chain diagram. He kept missing arrows. He closed the messages, finished the diagram carefully, and replied afterwards.
guided_check.prompt: Which statement best expresses the main idea?
options: Focusing on one task helped Mohan work accurately.
accepted_answers: Focusing on one task helped Mohan work accurately.

bridge.teaching_block: Find the change between before and after. The result after focusing is evidence for the central message.
bridge.passage: Nira switched between packing and reading, so she forgot her notebook. The next day she completed her packing list first and left with everything.
bridge.prompt: Which result supports the value of focus?

masterclass.teaching_block: A common mistake is choosing 'work without rest' as the message. Finishing one planned part before changing tasks still allows sensible breaks.
masterclass.passage: I finish one careful row, then stretch and rest; I start the next row when my hands feel their best.
masterclass.prompt: What advice does the verse give?
options: Complete a planned part, then take a sensible break.
accepted_answers: Complete a planned part, then take a sensible break.

independent_check.teaching_block: Interpret the new scene without a model answer.
independent_check.passage: Sonal was decorating a card while searching for a poem and sharpening pencils. Glue dried on the wrong side. She then chose the poem, completed the card, and sharpened the pencils last.
independent_check.prompt: State the main message and cite the detail that proves it.

concept_slots.description: states that handling one task at a time improves work
mentions the mistake during switching or successful ordered completion

transfer_check.teaching_block: Apply the focus message to a performance setting.
transfer_check.passage: During rehearsal, a tabla player watched the audience and missed the rhythm. She looked at the conductor, counted the beat, and played her section steadily.
transfer_check.prompt: Explain what changed and what lesson the event gives.

concept_slots.description: states that she shifted attention to the conductor or beat
mentions steady or improved playing
expresses that focus supports better performance

levels.title: Use sound and sense in short verse
levels.focus: identify rhymes and infer a focus word from poetic context
levels.teaching_goal: Recognise matching end sounds and use nearby actions to infer vocabulary meaning.

guided_check.teaching_block: Rhyming words share an ending sound, even when their first letters differ. Slow and glow end with the same long o sound.
guided_check.passage: Work slowly, row by row; / Soon your careful page will glow.

bridge.teaching_block: Say only the final sounds. Bright and right rhyme because both end with the same sound.
bridge.passage: Choose your task and hold it tight; / Finish well before the night.
bridge.prompt: Which two words form the end rhyme?

masterclass.teaching_block: Words do not rhyme merely because their spellings look alike. Move and love end differently; done and sun share a sound.
masterclass.passage: One job done beneath the sun; / Mark it complete, then choose task two.
masterclass.prompt: Which pair creates the clearest rhyme?

independent_check.teaching_block: Read the fresh couplet for both sound and meaning.
independent_check.passage: Do not scatter thought away; / Give one careful task its day.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use context to interpret a focus word in prose.
transfer_check.passage: During the model build, Eshan ignored side conversations and kept his attention on fitting the wheels. His concentration helped him finish.

levels.title: Describe what is happening now
levels.focus: use is or are with an -ing verb in context
levels.teaching_goal: Match a singular or plural subject with is or are and an -ing action to describe current work.

guided_check.teaching_block: Present continuous describes an action happening now. A singular subject takes is: 'Ravi is sorting.'
guided_check.passage: Ravi _____ sorting the index cards now.
guided_check.prompt: Which helping verb makes Ravi's current action correct?

bridge.teaching_block: First find the subject. A plural subject such as children takes are.
bridge.passage: The children _____ painting one panel at a time.

masterclass.teaching_block: Do not choose is just because the nearest noun is singular. The full subject controls agreement: 'The boxes on the shelf are falling.'
masterclass.passage: The stack of papers _____ sliding towards the edge.
masterclass.prompt: Which helping verb agrees with stack?

independent_check.teaching_block: Build the current-action form without choices.
independent_check.passage: Mina and Joel _____ checking the list now.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use present continuous in a community setting.
transfer_check.passage: The baker _____ weighing one bag of flour at the moment.
transfer_check.prompt: Complete the sentence with the helping verb and action word.

levels.title: Order tasks with clear connectors
levels.focus: arrange steps and use sequence connectors accurately
levels.teaching_goal: Use task dependencies and first, next, after, and finally to express a sensible order.

guided_check.teaching_block: Order depends on what each step needs. You must write the message before checking its spelling.
guided_check.passage: Steps: check spelling; write the invitation; place it in an envelope.

bridge.teaching_block: Ask which result becomes the starting point for the next action. After washing a cup, you can dry it.
bridge.passage: First wash the paint cup. _____ dry it. Finally return it to the shelf.
bridge.prompt: Which connector fits the second step?

masterclass.teaching_block: A common mistake is ordering by sentence length. Use cause and dependency: glue must be applied before pieces can stick.
masterclass.passage: Steps: press the paper pieces together; apply glue to the edges; let the model dry.
options: apply glue, press the pieces, let the model dry
press the pieces, let it dry, apply glue
let it dry, apply glue, press pieces
apply glue, let it dry, press pieces
accepted_answers: apply glue, press the pieces, let the model dry

independent_check.teaching_block: Arrange all steps without connector hints.
independent_check.passage: Steps: revise the draft; submit the story; write the first draft; read the instructions.
independent_check.prompt: Put the four steps in a sensible order.
accepted_answers: read the instructions, write the first draft, revise the draft, submit the story
read the instructions; write the first draft; revise the draft; submit the story
read instructions, write draft, revise draft, submit story

transfer_check.teaching_block: Sequence a simple repair outside school.
transfer_check.passage: Steps: test whether the torch works; insert fresh batteries; open the battery cover; close the cover.
accepted_answers: open the battery cover, insert fresh batteries, close the cover, test whether the torch works
open the battery cover; insert fresh batteries; close the cover; test whether the torch works
open cover, insert batteries, close cover, test torch

levels.title: Plan and explain a focused routine
levels.focus: summarise a busy situation and write a practical routine in own words
levels.teaching_goal: Write connected sentences that prioritise tasks, justify the order, and include a sensible transition or break.

guided_check.teaching_block: A useful routine names the order and gives a reason. Worked example: 'I will finish the reading first because it is due tomorrow. Then I will pack my art materials.'
guided_check.passage: Alia must complete a worksheet due tomorrow and label a box needed next week.
options: Finish the worksheet first, then label the box.
Label the box and ignore the worksheet.
accepted_answers: Finish the worksheet first, then label the box.

bridge.teaching_block: Make a plan by checking deadline, size, and dependency. The task needed soon usually comes first unless another step must precede it.
bridge.passage: Kartik must charge a camera before filming and choose music after filming.

masterclass.teaching_block: A focused routine is not simply a list. It explains a sensible order. Doing the easiest task first can be unhelpful when a required task has an earlier deadline.
masterclass.passage: A poem recitation is tomorrow; a scrapbook is due next month.
masterclass.prompt: Which plan best handles the deadlines?
options: Practise the recitation, then work on the scrapbook.
Decorate the scrapbook all evening and skip practice.
Begin both tasks at the same second.
accepted_answers: Practise the recitation, then work on the scrapbook.

independent_check.teaching_block: Create an original routine rather than copying a sentence frame.
independent_check.passage: Before dinner, Dev must feed the dog, finish a maths page due tomorrow, and organise a shelf that can wait until Saturday.
independent_check.prompt: Write three connected sentences giving a sensible order and one reason.

concept_slots.description: places feeding the dog and/or due maths before the shelf
explains at least one priority
gives a connected routine of multiple actions

transfer_check.teaching_block: Plan focused work in a shared family event.
transfer_check.passage: A family meal begins at seven. Ritu must chill juice, set plates, and make paper decorations that are optional.
transfer_check.prompt: In your own words, write a short plan and explain one priority.

concept_slots.description: gives a sensible order for chilling juice and setting plates before optional decorations
explains time, chilling, or necessity
uses connected complete ideas

items.passage: Kavya kept leaving her puzzle to check the door. When she stayed with the puzzle, she saw the pattern and completed it.
items.prompt: Which statement sums up Kavya's puzzle experience?
options: Sustained attention helped Kavya solve the puzzle.
accepted_answers: Sustained attention helped Kavya solve the puzzle.

items.passage: Ritesh first tried to pack, eat, and search for keys together. He spilled juice. Then he ate, packed, and found the keys in order.
items.prompt: State the message and one supporting detail.

concept_slots.description: states that doing tasks in order prevents mistakes
mentions the spill or successful ordered actions

items.passage: A singer stopped reading side notes and watched the conductor. Her entry came at the correct beat.
items.prompt: Which detail supports the value of focused attention?
options: Her entry came at the correct beat.
accepted_answers: Her entry came at the correct beat.

items.passage: A carpenter measures one shelf, cuts it, and checks the fit before starting the next shelf.
items.prompt: Explain the work habit shown by this process.

concept_slots.description: identifies completing or checking one shelf before the next
connects the habit to accuracy or fit

items.passage: Keep the guiding marks in sight; / Finish every knot just right.
items.prompt: Which words rhyme?

items.passage: Plan one chore before you roam; / Finish it, then wander home.
items.prompt: Write the two end words that rhyme.

items.passage: The editor was attentive, noticing each missing full stop.
items.prompt: What does attentive mean?

items.passage: Mira persisted with the difficult stitch until the cloth was repaired.
items.prompt: Use the outcome to explain persisted.

items.passage: The mason _____ checking the wall now.
items.prompt: Choose the correct helping verb.

items.passage: Two nurses _____ preparing the room at the moment.
items.prompt: Supply the helping verb for the plural subject.

items.passage: The row of lamps _____ glowing beside the path.
items.prompt: Which verb agrees with the singular subject row?

items.passage: The volunteers _____ sorting blankets now.
items.prompt: Complete the current-action phrase.

items.passage: Steps: cool the cake; mix the batter; bake it; pour batter into the tin.
items.prompt: Which action comes first?

items.passage: Steps: hang the shirt; rinse it; wash it; let it dry.
items.prompt: Put the steps in logical order.
accepted_answers: wash it, rinse it, hang the shirt, let it dry
wash it; rinse it; hang the shirt; let it dry

items.passage: The ink was wet, _____ Pavi waited before turning the page.
items.prompt: Which connector links the wet ink to Pavi's decision?

items.passage: The plant looked dry because nobody had watered it. Asha checked the soil and then added water.
items.prompt: Explain the cause and the next sensible action.

concept_slots.description: states that lack of water made the plant dry
states that checking soil came before adding water

items.passage: A report is due tomorrow; a poster is due next Friday.
items.prompt: Which plan uses deadlines sensibly?
options: Complete the report before starting the poster.
Decorate the poster and ignore the report.
accepted_answers: Complete the report before starting the poster.

items.passage: Before leaving at eight, Nita must pack lunch, fill a bottle, and polish shoes that are already clean.
items.prompt: Write a short plan and justify one priority.

concept_slots.description: prioritises lunch and water over unnecessary polishing
explains time or necessity
uses connected actions

items.passage: A gardener must water wilting seedlings and repaint a sign that is still readable.
items.prompt: What should happen first?
options: Leave both jobs for a week.

items.passage: A student has twenty minutes to review spelling, sharpen pencils, and redesign a notebook cover.
items.prompt: In your own words, make a focused plan and explain the order.

concept_slots.description: places spelling review before optional cover redesign
includes sharpening pencils only as a brief useful step
explains time, importance, or upcoming need
